beats.title: World
beats.headline: Vatican City: Pope walking, Mass; Black Sea search ends.
beats.body:
Vatican City. Afternoon medical bulletin: blood tests and a chest X-ray after Tuesday’s lobe removal were within expected ranges; Pope Leo XIV has begun respiratory physiotherapy, walked in his room, and resumed normal meals (breakfast and lunch). Holy See Press Office director Matteo Bruni later said the Pope concelebrated Mass Wednesday afternoon in a specially prepared 10th-floor room at Gemelli. Peru’s president floated that next month’s Latin America trip might need adjusting; the Holy See has not changed the Nov. 6–17 plan.

Africa. Quiet beyond this morning’s Ethiopia–Eritrea / Kabila / Ebola / Mauritius file. Mauritius police said traffic was moving again Wednesday morning after the overnight curfew, with cabinet reviewing next steps; no fresh Zalambessa or FRN headline after the morning wire.

Asia. Indonesia’s wildfire haze pushed Singapore’s 1-hour PM2.5 to about 284 µg/m³ in the west—the year’s high so far—and East Timor suspended in-person classes for three days from Oct. 15. China–North Korea’s New Yalu River Bridge still opens Thursday as planned.

Europe. Bulgaria abandoned the search for the missing HS Dignity crew at 3 p.m. local Wednesday after weather (gusts to 72 km/h, force-5 seas) halted the resumed Navy survey; six had been rescued Tuesday. Black Sea security still heads to the Oct. 15–16 European Council.

North America. September CPI printed hot: +0.6% month / 3.7% year (core +0.3% / 2.6%), with gasoline up 9.1% driving about half the monthly gain. Hurricane Simon weakened to a Category 1 (~75 mph) and drifted southwest ~270 miles SSE of Cabo San Lucas; Baja still on watch for watches/warnings.

South America. Escondida supervisors ratified BHP’s offer (~64% yes), sealing a 36-month contract and averting the strike that had been hanging over the world’s biggest copper mine.

Oceania. Quiet since this morning’s Pacific UN sea-level note and Gold Coast Norwell bushfire watch.

beats.body: Quiet for stockholders beyond this morning’s Roadster and FSD Lite notes. Tesla’s next-gen Roadster livestream remains Thursday, Oct. 15, 7:55 p.m. Central outdoors in Texas (SpaceX cold-gas thruster demo teased). CRS-35 Dragon still frames Thursday docking (see NASA). No fresh FSD or Starship delta after morning.

beats.title: NASA
beats.headline: Crew preps; CRS-35 docking still ~11 a.m. Thursday.
beats.body: Station. Wednesday’s station blog: Expedition 75 is prepping for Dragon’s arrival while running vision and robotics research; flight engineers Anil Menon and Joshua Kutryk will monitor the automated approach. NASA+ coverage still starts 9:15 a.m. EDT Thursday for the ~11 a.m. Harmony zenith docking (iROSA pair, spacesuit, retina and heart-tissue research aboard). Mars sample-return path unchanged from this morning’s note.

beats.title: Catholic
beats.headline: Pope Mass at Gemelli; Miami still Acutis Friday.
beats.body:
Miami. No new clergy assignments posted since morning. Archbishop Wenski’s prayer ask still stands; Friday’s St. Carlo Acutis Eucharistic Miracles Exposition at St. Mark (Southwest Ranches) remains the weekend’s local highlight. Quiet otherwise on parish calendars beyond Emmaus / Gettys notes already briefed.

Rome / worldwide. Biggest Church delta is the Pope’s afternoon recovery bulletin and hospital Mass (see World). Morning’s Košice and Cuiabá archbishop nominations and Tagle’s Amoris Laetitia Mass still the day’s appointment/liturgy file; no fresh Bollettino reassignments after the Oct. 14 list.

beats.title: Signs of the times
beats.headline: Countdown still Oct. 3; Sept. 25 Medjugorje stands.
beats.body:
Countdown to the Kingdom. Rechecked this evening: nothing newer than Oct. 3—Marija’s “Time of Prayer for Peace,” Elizabeth Kindelmann (“Satan Will be Blinded”), and Pedro Regis (“Humanity is Sick”).

Latest Marian message. Our Lady’s Sept. 25 Medjugorje message through Marija remains the newest monthly message: a time of prayer for peace, with families asked to renew the Rosary. October’s 25th message is not out yet.

Prayer signs. The Pope’s hospital Mass and continued recovery prayers (see Catholic / World) are tonight’s clearest living sign; Friday’s Acutis exposition still the local Eucharistic marker. No sober new chip or digital-ID headline worth elevating.

beats.body:
Tonight: Heat host Brooklyn at Kaseya Center (tip 7:30 p.m. ET)—early first quarter had Miami up 17–14; final in Pick-me-up when the clock stops.

Friday–Sunday: Same family/Christian slate as morning—Acutis exposition at St. Mark (Southwest Ranches), Food Trucks Friday at Tropical Park, Schott 5K Saturday, Gettys at Coral Ridge Presbyterian Sunday 4–6 p.m. No new family-event headline after morning.

beats.title: Pick-me-up
beats.headline: Heat lead Nets early; Roadster and D&D still tomorrow/’27.
beats.body: At briefing time the Heat led Brooklyn 17–14 in the first quarter at Kaseya Center (preseason tip 7:30 p.m. ET)—game still live, so check the final after the horn; Orlando Friday closes the exhibition slate. Star Wars side stays fun from morning’s NYCC drop: D&D | Star Wars Core Rules plus Tyro Squadron still aimed at 2027. Tomorrow’s Tesla Roadster livestream is the other pop-culture countdown if you want a lighter Thursday night.
